source: Of course it isn't genuine. That young Fortinbras was trying to make war on us all just last week!
You're always so suspicious, Irma.
Only of those who have wanted to kill us in the past. Or whose parents we have killed.
Or in this case, both.
It is right to be suspicious. Suspicion of every one, and every thing, is the only reason I survive.
That aside, I believe that today's meal will be to your liking. The men brought home a boar from the hunt.
I've also stewed some kohlrabi. For old times' sake. Just the sort I made for you when you were a girl.
Truly? But you know the others don't care for them!
Hm. A pity. I guess you'll have to eat them all yourself.
I suppose I will.
Hello again, Irma.
How are you getting by, my lady? Are your spirits high?
I'm managing all right. Nothing I can't handle.
Do you have any more of that kohlrabi?
Things have been sort of trying these last few weeks. But eating these brought me comfort that everything might be all right. I felt like I was a girl again.
Hamlet acting up again?
Yes. I'm out of ideas.
If you need to borrow one of my spoons, I give you my blessing. I'm sure you could put it to good use.
Could even help straighten out the Prince.
I'm still hoping it's just a phase. I'm sure it will pass. But your offer is, as always, very kind.
I am sorry about Hamlet, my dear Gerta.
Although the boy had his edges, he is gone too soon.
It's still dawning on me that he's dead. It's like I haven't quite believed it.
You've lost a child. You know what it's like. How do I live through this?
You don't. A part of you dies.
The part of you that dreamed of embracing them on their wedding day, of watching them grow old, bear children of their own...
That part of you is gone forever.
But the rest of you somehow carries on. And so shall you, little Gerta. So shall you.
This one is a little crooked.
Such a lovely painting. I wonder what your story is?
Finally, some peace and--
Oh, wonderful, it's you. Can't a girl admire art in peace?
I wasn't aware you had such a connection to the royal gallery.
You're not aware of much, really, so that's not surprising.
What brings you in here, then?
I enjoy the excuse to be in here, away from the noise.
Things are so emotional in the court lately. You'd think royalty would be raised better.
You mean Hamlet?
Yes. Don't you hear what he says about you?
It's always, 'Ophelia said this!' and 'Ophelia said that!' and 'Get her to a nunnery!' and the like. He can be so tedious.
And now with Hamlet dead, things have only devolved.
I often come here simply to escape everyone. You included, obviously.
For what little it's worth, I like to hide away sometimes, too.
Would that we were born men, Ophelia, and had nothing to hide from.
Look at these beautiful works. Nothing about the artist's will is hidden. He paints beautifully, every expression exquisite in its uniqueness.
The colors are incredible. It's as though he's reaching through the frame to grab you by the hand and say, I cannot be ignored.
I've never looked at these paintings that closely before, I suppose.
I sit here, a golden idiot, idling at the Queen's side. And I brush her hair and listen to her chatter. And it's all...
If I were born a man, I would paint and fight and run free. And I would go as far as my feet could take me.
A-anyhow. No sense telling you in all of that. Begone. De-summon. How do I banish you?
Oh, never mind. I'll go. Bye.
She seems, ah, unusually distressed. I wonder if anyone else in the castle knows why.
Who were you?
Astrid. Queen Astrid.
Such a sad, longing face for a Queen.
And such beautiful color work. True artistry.
I wonder if I could replicate this technique.
Who are you talking to?
Not you, 'Feely.
Did I ask to be accosted? Why are you here?
You sound lonely, for a girl who has the company of the Queen herself.
Yes, well.
The company of a Queen means very little. Ask Astrid herself. Ah, right, you can't. Because she's dead.
Ophelia? Dear?
What is it, Father?
I need you to come with me. Quickly, now.
Father. King Claudius. Do as you will.
Are you certain you want to see this through, my lord?
As we discussed earlier, her mind's not well. She needs help.
It's what's best for her. You know that to be true, Polonius.
I'm sorry. I'm so sorry, Ophelia. But everything you've been saying-- these visions--
I don't want any harm to come to you. We'll only send you away for a little while. I promise.
I'll ensure she's delivered with all the care my men can provide. We'll watch over her, my lord.
Thank you, Bernardo.
A prison there, or a slightly larger prison here. What difference does it make?
Both are the box that was built just for me.
What is this? What's going on?
Do as you will.
Oh, no.
It's what's best for her, Polonius.
I'm not delusional, Father. Don't do this.
You're sending me to an asylum? Really?
I'm sorry. I'm so sorry. But everything you've been saying-- these visions--
I don't want any harm to come to you. It'll only be for a little while. I promise.
I was telling you the truth. If you won't believe me, why not just let me go?
What is--
Oh no.
No, no, no-- this again?
Stop her!
Bernardo, give her the dwale. I can't bear to see her like this.
Come and drink this, my lady.
Stay away from me!
Why does this keep happening? I'm trying to save you all!
Ophelia. Don't fight me. Please.
Things will be better on the other side, my love.
You'll be safe. Nothing will harm you there.
I could use the Book of Fates to embrace madness, if I wanted to.
I tried. I tried to tell them. But they wouldn't believe me.

source: What was that play about, Hamlet?
I've been asking myself the same question.
Were you upset by it?
In a number of ways, yes.
Listen. Meet me at midnight. There's something I want to discuss, but this courtyard is neither the time nor the place.
Then I have just the place in mind.
My personal chambers are far from the King's ears.
Perfect. When I'm done attending to the Queen, I'll come see you.
About that play earlier.
Enough about the play. I ought to have Quince expelled from Elsinore for changing the script I wrote.
So you didn't write that script?
No. Someone else changed the bloody play.
All this after Quince and I had an agreement.
Is that what you came here to ask me about? You look white with rage.
No, no, it's nothing.
Brit. Why are you shaking so?
Do you know something about the spy's identity?
I think we all do.
Now no one will disturb us.
(She barred the door?)
Hamlet. We should leave. Now.
In a moment. I want to understand first.
Hold your tongue if you value your life.
So it is you. You're the spy.
And here I thought you were at Elsinore to serve my mother.
You're as much a liar as everyone else in this castle!
I warned you.
Ophelia was right. You should have run.
But you never could listen to anyone, could you? Poor idiot.
You knew about me, and you didn't go to Bernardo. I don't know why, but I know you're a threat.
You. You orchestrated that performance somehow, didn't you?
Wait, Brit. We can discuss this.
No. We can't.
Only you had to die. His death was unnecessary.
Now I'm going to have to explain to all of them how Hamlet attacked you, and I had no choice but to turn on him.
Lovers' spats can turn violent so quickly, after all.
I didn't want to do this. To do any of this.
They'll all believe her lies. I know they will.

source: I don't think the explanation matters. You're committing treason. That's all I care about.
I fought to tell Fortinbras I wasn't going to be a killer on his behalf. But that performance was...
I don't know how you knew all of that. It's like you were inside my head. What are you?
I didn't want to kill you. I still don't. But that performance...
They'll all believe her lie. I know they will.

context.type: 资料、界面或未定位对白

source: I'm sorry, Brit.
For what?
I know you wouldn't be doing this unless you felt you had no other choice.
Doing 'this?'
You're about to kill me. I don't blame you. But you know you're being used. By your father, by Fortinbras.
Don't act as though you know me! You don't know a damn thing about what I've been through!
She's wrong. I know exactly what she's been through. But that's not enough to save her.

source: How could you change the play, Quince? We we had a deal!
A deal? What an interesting interpretation of my words!
You merely had some suggested material for rewriting the performance. I elected not to follow that material.
It's more than that. Someone else is giving you orders. Your play was a mockery of me.
Who talked to you? Are you working with Claudius?
Who talked to you?
I act of my own free will. The same cannot, of course, be said for you.
If he's trying to drive me insane, it's working. I can't do this anymore.
E-everyone's against me--
Everyone's laughing at me now.
You don't understand! I had things riding on that performance. Now it's all for nothing.
You can't control art, Hamlet. My muse told me to go in a different direction, so I did.
Now please, leave me alone. Putting on a performance of this caliber can be quite draining.
Father. Are you there?
Show yourself. I know you're listening.
My brother lives.
You had every chance to extinguish him.
I had a plan, Father. I was going to reveal him before the entire court. But it failed.
I am a failure. I look the fool.
My son. Remember what I told you in life: One must prevail until no other possible method remains.
Father, the mantle of my life is crushing me beneath its weight. I want to die. I want to stop the pain so badly, Father. I'd do anything.
I know, my son.
I can sense that you are in the throes of darkness.
And I've disappointed you, too.
I'm... I'm sorry.
Hamlet. What are you doing up here?
Where are the others? Does anyone else know you're up here?
Hamlet. I came to convince you not to give up.
I failed everyone. I failed to protect my father's life and to avenge him of his killer.
I'm the laughingstock of everyone I've ever known and loved. Even my closest friends have turned on me.
Hamlet, stop!
Please, stop, I beg of you!
Mother. Go away.
